item.title: Lateral Raises DO"S &DONT'S
item.description:
Feeling the lateral raise in your traps instead of your delts?
Save this post & use this cue next time you perform the side (lateral) raise 👇🏻
A lot of people initiate the movement by shrugging the shoulders when:
1. The weights are too heavy • 2. They’ve been executing it poorly from the beginning
Next time you perform the lateral raise, instead of thinking of lifting the dumbbells “up”, think of lifting the dumbbells “out”, like you are dragging them against the walls.
You don’t need heavy weights for this movement!
Your traps will still be involved to some degree in this movement, but your delts should be doing most of the work!

Both movements are different variations of the functional ‘Push’ movement. The Dumbbell Bench Press is an example of horizontal pushing, which targets the chest and triceps more; whereas the Dumbbell Shoulder Press is an example of the vertical pushing, which targets the shoulders and triceps more.

item.title: ✅ The PERFECT Overhead Dumbbell Triceps Extension
item.description:
✅ The PERFECT Overhead Dumbbell Triceps Extension
1️⃣ Adjust Your Seat Position – Slide your butt slightly forward on the shoulder press seat so your torso leans back. This sets you up for better arm positioning in the next step.
2️⃣ Angle Your Upper Arms Slightly Back – Instead of keeping them completely vertical, let your upper arms tilt slightly backward. This adjustment keeps constant tension on your triceps and increases the effective range of motion, allowing you to lower the dumbbell further.
3️⃣ Tuck Your Elbows – Keep your elbows close to your head rather than flaring them out. This maintains tension on the triceps and reduces unnecessary strain on your elbows. @deltabolic

item.title: While doing the chest press machine with a low seat setting #chest #pecs #chestmuscles
item.description:
While doing the chest press machine with a low seat setting, there’s a potential hazard of executing the exercise at a 90-degree angle.
This situation can increase the likelihood of shoulder injuries and diminish the activation of your chest muscles.
To avert this, it is recommended to elevate the seat to a higher setting. This adjustment enables you to keep your elbows at approximately a 75-degree angle, encouraging more secure shoulder motion and enhancing the involvement of your chest muscles throughout the workout.
